title: True branch of a conditional run
statement: Let $L$ be resource limits, $c$ a condition, $s,t$ statements, $\sigma$ a state, and $R$ a predicate on states. If $s$ is block-safe from $\sigma$ and its resulting state satisfies $R$, if $c$ holds in $\sigma$, and if $c$ is safe under $L$ in $\sigma$, then the conditional with branches $s,t$ is block-safe from $\sigma$ and its resulting state satisfies $R$.
hypotheses_covered: The true branch $s$ runs safely from $\sigma$ to $R$ under $L$
The condition is safe under $L$ in $\sigma$
replaced:
Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be a set of word, space, and depth bounds; let $\sigma$ be a program
state; let $R$ be a property of states; and let $c$ be a condition with two statements
$s,t$ as its branches. A statement runs safely from a state to $R$ when it is block-safe
there and its resulting state satisfies $R$. If $s$ runs safely from $\sigma$ to $R$,
the condition is safe at $\sigma$, and the condition is true at $\sigma$, then the
conditional statement with branches $s,t$ runs safely from $\sigma$ to $R$.
